Fetal Development and Genetics

Figure 3-13    Female reproductive cycle: interrelationships 
of hormones with the four phases of the uterine cycle and the 
two phases of the ovarian cycle in an ideal 28-day cycle.

Two Ovarian Phases 
 The follicular phase (days 1–14)
 Follicle matures and ovulation occurs.
 ESTROGEN IS PRIMARY HORMONE
 The luteal phase (days 15–28)
 Begins when the ovum leaves the follicle, and the 
corpus luteum develops from the ruptured follicle.
 PROGESTERONE IS PRIMARY HORMONE

Four Uterine Phases 
 Menstrual: day 1-6 Menses 
 Proliferative: day 7-14 Preparation of uterine 
lining for implantation of fertilized egg
OVULATION AT DAY 14 (corpus luteum forms in 
ovary from released ovum)
 Secretory: Corpus Luteum produces 
progesterone to support pregnancy 
 Ischemic: begins at day 26 if no fertilized 
ovum ends at menses
 Menses begins approximately 2 days later (day 28 aka 
day 1)

Proliferative Phase
 The endometrial cells enlarge and become twisted under 
the influence of estrogen, and the endometrium thickens.
Secretory Phase
 Progesterone causes marked swelling and the amount of 
tissue glycogen increases.
 Vascularity of the entire uterus increases greatly, providing 
a nourishing bed for implantation
Ischemic Phase
 Corpus luteum begins to degenerate.
 Estrogen and progesterone levels fall.
 This phase is characterized by the escape of blood into the 
stromal cells of the uterus.

Ovulation, the ovum leaves the ovary and enters the fallopian 
tube. Fertilization occurs in the outer third of the fallopian tube.

Stages of Fetal Development
 Preembryonic stage:  fertilization (union of ova and sperm to form 
Zygote) through 2nd week.
 Fertilization; cleavage (divisions); morula = 16 cells
 Blastocyst- inner cell mass that forms embryo and amnion
 Trophoblast-outer cell mass that forms placenta and chorion
 Implantation occurs at day 7-10
Blastocyst-differentiates into:
Ectoderm-forms central nervous system
Mesoderm-skeletal, urinary, circulatory and reproductive 
systems
Endoderm- respiratory, liver, pancreas and digestive 
system

Embryonic Layers 
 Ectoderm: forms the central nervous system, special 
senses, skin and glands
 Mesoderm: forms skeletal, urinary, circulatory, and 
reproductive organs 
 Endoderm: forms respiratory system, liver, pancreas, 
and digestive system

Fetal Development
 Embryonic stage:  end of 2nd week through 8th week
 Basic structures of major body organs and main external 
features
 Embryonic membranes form 
 Chorion outermost embryonic layer-will project into the uterine 
wall.  Chorionic villi on the surface bring oxygen and nutrition to 
embryo/fetus
• Amnion- rises from 
ectoderm: fluid filled to 
protect embryo
• Expands with embryonic 
growth to touch chorion-
forming amniotic sac (bag of 
waters surrounding embryo)

Fetal stage:  end of the 8th week until birth 
 Pregnancy- 280 days from Last Menstrual Period (LMP)
 Growth and development of differentiated systems
 Fetal Circulation Begins
Formation of fraternal twins with separate placentas
Formation of identical twins.

Amniotic Fluid
 Surrounds and protects embryo and fetus
 Derived from two sources
 Fluid transport across amnion from maternal blood
 Fetal urine production
 Protects umbilical cord from compression
 Temperature regulation for fetus
 Cushioning fetus from trauma
 Volume changes during pregnancy
 Adequacy of volume is indicator of fetal well being

The Placenta
 The interface between the mother and fetus
 Making hormones to control the physiology of the 
mother
 Protecting the fetus from immune attack by the mother
 Removing waste products from the fetus
 Inducing the mother to bring more food to the placenta
 Producing hormones that mature into fetal organs

Hormonal Functions of Pregnancy
 hCG: Produced by trophoblast and later by the placenta to 
support pregnancy. Presence of hCG is basis of + 
pregnancy test
 Human placental lactogen (hPL) : 
 Decreases insulin receptor sensitivity to keep glucose 
available for fetal development.
 Prepares mammary glands to produce milk
 Estrogen: 
 Prevent ovulation (suppress FSH) and LH
 Uterine expansion and pliability for labor
 Progesterone: 
 Maintain uterine lining
 Prevents maternal rejection of embryo (used as 
treatment for women with hx of unexplained 1st 
trimester pregnancy loss)
 Relaxin: Allows pelvis expansion through loosening of 
ligaments. May result in achy joints and “waddle” of 
pregnancy

Umbilical Cord
 Formed from the amnion
 Lifeline from the mother to the growing embryo
 Contains one large vein and two small arteries
 Wharton’s jelly surrounds the vein and arteries 
to prevent compression
 At term, the average umbilical cord is 22 inches 
long and about 1 inch wide

Role of Amniotic Fluid
 Helps maintain a constant body temperature for the 
fetus
 Permits symmetric growth and development
 Cushions the fetus from trauma
 Allows the umbilical cord to be relatively free of 
compression
 Promotes fetal movement to enhance musculoskeletal 
development

Fetal Circulation
 Blood from the placenta to and through the fetus 
and then back to placenta 
 Three shunts during fetal life:
 Ductus venosus: connects the umbilical vein to 
the inferior vena cava
 Ductus arteriosus: connects the main pulmonary 
artery to the aorta
 Foramen ovale: anatomic opening between the 
right and left atrium

Fetal Circulation
 https://youtu.be/Mdid3gLfzBk?si=iP4bi0OuuCSJRN0Q

Fetal Circulation- Maternal blood flows through the uterine arteries 
to the intervillous spaces of the placenta and returns through the 
uterine veins to maternal circulation. Fetal blood flows through the 
umbilical arteries into the villous capillaries of the placenta and 
returns through the umbilical vein to the fetal circulation.

Common Prenatal Genetic Testing 
NIPT: Non-invasive prenatal testing
 cfDNA: Maternal serum for fetal cell fragments (micro DNA deletions)
 10-11 weeks: screen for chromosomal abnormalities
 Fetal Nuchal Translucency- 10-14 wks Intravaginal ultrasound-of fluid in neonatal cervical spine- 
>2.5 mm = abnormal- Trisomies 13/18/21, Turners syndrome
 Triple/Quad screen Alpha-fetoprotein-Maternal blood .
15-18 wks pregnancy.  High rates of false positives
 Increased=neural tube defect Decreased=Trisomy 18 & 21
Invasive Testing
 Chorionic Villi Sampling CVS Transvaginal fetal placental tissue. 10-12 wks.  Direct fetal 
chromosomal sample
 Amniocentesis- Aspiration of amniotic fluid. 15-20 wks
 Direct chromosome analysis 2-4 wks for results
 Risk of infection, spontaneous AB, 
 DNA markers, CF, Tay-Sachs, sickle cell
 Percutaneous Umbilical Sampling- 16 wks diagnosis of fetal blood disorders, infection, treatment of 
isoimmunization
